sections.heading: 4. Prove readiness with a funded order and a reversible failure drill
paragraphs: Run one complete dry transaction before introducing live customer funds. Choose a supplier-supported test environment where available; otherwise use internal records and clearly separated synthetic orders that never submit purchases. Create a customer identifier, capture authority, attach a quote, calculate retained revenue, simulate collection, and reconcile the supplier statement. For a $10,000 customer invoice with $9,000 attributable supplier cost under an applicable agency arrangement, the spread is $1,000, not $10,000 of scorecard revenue. At the matrix's domestic card planning rate, collection costs $290.30, leaving $709.70 before other operating costs; capped ACH processing would cost $5 under the stated schedule, leaving $995. Actual authorization, settlement timing, return exposure, and account pricing still determine the collection design. Do not extrapolate those illustrative contribution figures into replacement annual scorecard margins. Then replay the same statement and webhook identifiers to prove that no duplicate invoice, seat order, or commission is created. An operator should be able to trace every amount from signed terms through earning evidence to the bank entry without joining records by customer display name. Preserve the dry-run artifacts as the template for first-deal review.

Exercise the failures that can overwhelm a small team: an ACH return after provisioning, a duplicate supplier statement, a compressed partner rebate, a lost administrator device, and a customer requesting an unsupported transfer. Assign each failure a person, a response deadline, and a bounded financial exposure. A $50,000 eligible monthly spend base at a 4% retained rebate produces $2,000; compression to 3% removes $500 monthly, or $6,000 annually if sustained. That loss must reduce forecast contribution unless contract terms or operating changes genuinely offset it. Test recovery by restoring evidence and the SQLite database into a clean environment, then checking record counts, hashes, and access restrictions. Set an initial recovery-point target of one business day and a recovery-time target of four business hours for internal records; do not advertise these as supplier-backed service commitments. Revoke a test worker's access and verify loss of vault, mailbox, CRM, and cloud permissions. Keep emergency credentials offline with controlled access. A backup that cannot be restored and an account that cannot be revoked are production defects, even when the subscription invoice is only a few dollars.

Release the first live order only after commercial authority, funding sufficiency, revenue mapping, and recovery evidence all pass the checks below. For the first thirty days, review supplier liabilities and settled collections daily, exceptions twice weekly, and acquisition economics weekly. Keep the founder responsible for supplier commitments; contractors can research public signals, reconcile approved statements, and prepare customer documentation within scoped permissions. Expand fixed spend only after recurring retained contribution covers the proposed recurring expense and the reserve remains intact under a payout delay. If a $300 monthly automation service saves six hours at $40 per hour, its $240 labor benefit does not justify the purchase on labor savings alone. Measure additional error reduction separately rather than asserting it. Keep a twelve-week cash forecast with dated receipts, contractual supplier debits, payroll, contractor milestones, and rebate-reversal scenarios. Reconcile the forecast to actual bank activity every week and record why each material variance occurred. A lean launch is complete when a funded, authorized transaction can be collected, fulfilled, reconciled, and recovered by the assigned team without improvisation. It is not complete merely because twelve vendor accounts exist or a dashboard shows a large pipeline.

sop_steps.action: Run a synthetic order through fees, settlement, and statement matching.

sop_steps.action: Approve the order only after all four readiness proofs pass.
sop_steps.detail: Inspect the first settlement and supplier liability manually, retain the evidence, and resolve exceptions before increasing volume.

chapters.subtitle: Microsoft NCE Credit Exposure, CSP Attribution Defects, VIP Entitlements, GPO Rebate Recapture, and SEC-Triggered Outreach Controls
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #37, ranked #04 of 37 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, wins through retained software spreads, residual commissions, GPO rebates, and verified renewal savings, not subscription billings disguised as revenue. Across the volume's 12 mapped plays, newcomer losses cluster around annual commitment exposure, defective partner attribution, unauthorized seat pooling, retroactive rebate changes, and acquisition practices that outrun evidence. The canonical annual owner profit cases are $32,000 Conservative, $225,000 Base, and $522,000 Scaled. This chapter converts those risks into contract checks, exposure limits, reconciliation tests, and stop-work rules. The question's 80% framing is a stress-test prompt, not an observed failure rate. Protect capital by measuring collectible contribution after reversals before expanding any apparently profitable channel.

sections.heading: 1. Cap Annual Commitments Before Selling Monthly Convenience
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is selling a payment schedule as if it changed the underlying commitment. Microsoft NCE annual subscriptions billed monthly can leave the transacting reseller owing the distributor after the customer stops paying. Under an illustrative contract, 100 seats at a $20 monthly wholesale cost create $24,000 of annual supplier obligations. Billing the customer $22 per seat produces only $2,400 of annual spread before servicing costs. If the customer pays three months and defaults, nine remaining supplier installments total $18,000, versus $600 of spread collected during those first three months. An enforceable customer promise does not fund tomorrow's supplier debit. Require annual prefunding wherever possible, verify settlement before activating the commitment, and treat ACH mandates or stored cards as collection mechanisms rather than credit protection. Measure uncovered exposure as remaining noncancelable supplier obligations minus specifically allocable settled customer funds and collectible contractual protection. Do not subtract expected future customer payments. A startup with $15,000 of available capital cannot safely absorb this example merely because its projected margin is positive. If prefunding fails, offer an available monthly commitment, use a documented referral-only structure, or decline the transaction instead of becoming an accidental lender.

The second trap is confusing relationship attribution with authority to transfer subscriptions or receive compensation. CPOR is not a universal billing-transfer instruction, and a customer relationship record does not automatically establish CSP resale rights. Confirm the exact Microsoft workload, partner program, transacting entity, customer acceptance, and distributor procedure before promising a migration date. Adobe VIP Marketplace transfers likewise depend on the applicable agreement, reseller process, anniversary timing, and eligible entitlements. The third trap is unauthorized cross-customer seat pooling: a spreadsheet showing unused licenses does not permit assignment across unrelated organizations. Keep each customer's tenant, subscription identifiers, purchased quantities, assignments, and approved reseller relationships separately traceable. At 400 seats and a $1.50 monthly retained spread, annual contribution is $7,200; a $12,000 contractual audit settlement consumes more than twenty months of that contribution before remediation labor. Never model the settlement as a published vendor penalty schedule; actual remedies follow the executed terms and established facts. Reject synthetic member companies, borrowed partner identifiers, educational-license laundering, and fabricated customer acceptance. The fallback is an authorized transfer or separate customer agreement, even when that sacrifices the volume bracket. Losing a discount is cheaper than losing the right to transact.

The fourth trap is assuming cancellations, seat reductions, renewals, and suspensions share one reversible workflow. Record the applicable Microsoft NCE cancellation window from current program terms and the distributor's accepted order record; do not assume a generic refund period or that suspension extinguishes the commitment. Store order timestamps in UTC, renewal settings, quantity-change deadlines, and evidence that the customer approved the precise term. Run a daily renewal queue at 90, 60, 30, and seven days, with an earlier internal deadline wherever the supplier requires it. One mistaken renewal of 250 seats at $18 wholesale monthly creates $54,000 of annual obligations. A $2 monthly spread on those seats would generate only $6,000 annually, so the contractual exposure is nine times the expected spread. Set a proposed startup limit of uncovered commitments below 25% of unrestricted cash, plus a separate prohibition on any single customer exceeding that limit. These are internal risk limits, not vendor rules. If the queue is incomplete, stop new annual orders rather than rushing transfers. Preserve service continuity through supplier support and customer coordination; never delete tenant data or use administrative access as improvised debt collection leverage.

sections.heading: 2. Reconstruct Every Rebate, Residual, and Savings Dollar
paragraphs: The fifth trap is pricing from the highest rebate tier before earning its conditions. Separate contractual wholesale spread from conditional incentives, and version the partner schedule used for every quote. Suppose eligible annual client purchases are $600,000 and a GPO administrative rebate is 2%; the potential operator receipt is $12,000, not $600,000. If returns and excluded product categories reduce eligible purchases to $450,000, the same rate produces $9,000. If the agreement instead applies a lower 1% tier retroactively at that volume, the receipt becomes $4,500. The $7,500 difference from the original expectation can erase an entire acquisition cohort's contribution. Document whether tiers are incremental or retroactive, whether affiliated members aggregate, which products qualify, and whether the administrative fee belongs to the GPO or is shared with members. Maintain a provisional rebate ledger until eligibility and measurement conditions support recognition. Monitor qualified volume against the relevant threshold weekly, using actual accepted purchases rather than proposals. If volume falls within 10% above a critical threshold, forecast both adjacent tiers and stop subsidizing customer prices with the higher tier. The fallback is a viable unconditional spread, not fictitious member enrollment or purchases manufactured solely to cross the bracket.

The sixth trap is treating an evergreen commission as an unconditional annuity. Telarus or Avant arrangements for Zoom and other UCaaS services depend on executed supplier and agent terms, eligible service charges, attribution, collections, and reversal provisions. An illustrative $20,000 monthly eligible billing base at a 10% commission rate yields $2,000 monthly operator revenue before any upstream split. If the operator retains 70% of that commission, retained revenue is $1,400, not $2,000 and certainly not $20,000. A cancellation that reverses three months of retained commissions creates a $4,200 exposure under that assumed clause. Do not substitute this example for a distributor's actual recovery schedule. The seventh trap is paying sales contractors immediately while the operator remains exposed to later chargebacks. Tie contractor payouts to collectible receipts and documented reversal allocation, with a lawful written recovery mechanism rather than arbitrary deductions. Track billed, eligible, earned, received, and reversible amounts separately. Investigate a commission variance exceeding 2% of expected retained receipts or any missing customer identifier before releasing the related payout. Where attribution remains disputed, stop advancing commissions, preserve correspondence, and escalate through the designated master-agent channel without attempting duplicate registrations under another identity.

The eighth trap is charging shared savings against a fabricated baseline. Define the comparison basket before negotiation: exact SKUs, licensed quantities, service levels, currency, taxes, contract term, credits, and implementation charges. With comparable annual spend falling from $120,000 to $96,000, verified savings are $24,000 and a 30% contingent fee is $7,200. If $8,000 of the apparent reduction comes from removing seats the customer had already scheduled to cancel, incremental negotiated savings are only $16,000 under a contract excluding preplanned removals, producing a $4,800 fee. The ninth trap is collecting both supplier compensation and a customer fee while concealing the overlap or counting the same benefit twice. Disclose the compensation structure and implement the agreed offset or credit treatment. Keep the baseline signed, vendor quotes preserved, realized invoices matched, and disputes tied to particular line items. If verification covers less than 95% of the claimed savings amount, hold the disputed portion instead of billing the full forecast. Use a fixed diagnostic fee only when separately agreed and actually earned. A defensible savings ledger protects both collection and renewal trust; an impressive percentage without a stable denominator creates a future refund demand.

callout.title: Veteran Controls That Keep Small Spreads Collectible
callout.body: Experienced operators preserve evidence at the moment terms are accepted, then reconcile economic rights separately from cash timing.
items: Snapshot the distributor quote, partner schedule, and effective date together; a later portal screenshot cannot establish an earlier rebate entitlement.
Maintain residual cohorts by supplier, customer activation month, agent split, and reversal window so one problematic vintage cannot hide inside aggregate growth.
Negotiate a signed savings basket before contacting vendors, including preplanned seat reductions and the exact treatment of supplier-funded credits.
Match every GPO member purchase to its eligibility category and return status before using that purchase to support a higher volume bracket.

sections.heading: 3. Keep Trigger Intelligence From Becoming Outreach Liability
paragraphs: The tenth trap is letting trigger speed outrun source quality. The mapped play sec_edgar_8k_vendor_trigger_arbitrage uses SEC Form D and Form 8-K events to prioritize timely outreach, not to prove purchasing intent. Ingest available EDGAR RSS and supported JSON sources, retain accession numbers, and deduplicate amendments before routing a lead. Form D reports exempt offerings; amounts offered, amounts sold, and filing dates are different facts, and none establishes unrestricted cash available for software procurement. Item 5.02 covers specified director and officer events, Item 1.01 material definitive agreements, and Item 2.01 completed acquisitions or dispositions of assets. Read the filing before assigning a renewal hypothesis. For an illustrative 200-event monthly queue, a 20% qualification rate produces 40 accounts; a 10% meeting rate produces four meetings; a 25% close rate produces one customer. At $3,000 retained contribution before acquisition costs and $800 of research and outreach costs, expected cohort contribution is $2,200. If qualification falls to 5%, the same downstream rates yield 0.25 expected customers and $750 before acquisition costs, producing a $50 loss. Faster alerts cannot rescue a negative qualified cohort. Pause the segment and revise the event-to-need hypothesis rather than increasing message volume.

The eleventh trap is turning public-data access into aggressive scraping. Apply a shared token bucket capped at five requests per second across workers, identify the organization in the User-Agent, cache immutable filing documents, and honor SEC fair-access guidance. Five requests per second is the chapter's conservative operating cap, not a promise of unrestricted access. On throttling or access-denial responses, stop the affected fetches, honor server instructions, and use bounded backoff rather than rotating identities or addresses. Mirror SEC nightly bulk ZIP archives where published for the required dataset, together with published indexes for historical lookbacks; do not assume every filing type has an equivalent real-time JSON endpoint or nightly archive. Separate historical backfills from the live queue so neither starves the other. The sub-hour objective runs from detected filing availability to a reviewed, channel-eligible outreach draft, not guaranteed contact before all commercial databases. If the live feed fails, process the cached backlog and mark source freshness explicitly. DNS, MX, and SPF observations provide another weak signal: Microsoft mail routing does not establish seat count, license edition, reseller identity, or renewal date. Request customer-provided subscription evidence before pricing a transfer or claiming recoverable savings.

The twelfth trap is assuming business targeting exempts every message from channel rules. The TCPA, 47 U.S.C. 227, and implementing FCC rules distinguish technology, message type, destination, and consent; a business contact's mobile number does not become unrestricted because their employer appears in an SEC filing. Artificial or prerecorded voice campaigns need a separate rules analysis from individually placed live calls. The FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule also prohibits specified deceptive practices in business-to-business telemarketing; verify which additional provisions and recordkeeping duties apply to the actual campaign. For commercial email, implement accurate routing information, nondeceptive subjects, required sender identification and postal address, and a working opt-out under CAN-SPAM. Honor opt-outs within the statutory deadline and synchronize suppression across contractors immediately as an operating standard. Never pitch an SEC-triggered lead as if the SEC recommended the offer. Use vendor names to identify genuine services, not to imply an unearned partnership. At 100 contacts costing $8 each, a campaign already consumes $800 before complaint handling. One supported complaint involving impersonation or a suppression failure should pause that workflow immediately. The fallback is corrected, human-reviewed outreach through an eligible channel, not another sending domain or contractor identity.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile Retained Revenue and Trip Circuit-Breakers Early
paragraphs: The thirteenth trap is celebrating client subscription spend as operator revenue. The Formula v2.0 scorecard labels its top line gross revenue, but this candidate's specified basis is retained spreads, retained residuals, GPO administrative rebates, and shared-savings fees, excluding pass-through subscription spend. Apply any upstream split once at the relevant commission or fee layer. For example, $100,000 of eligible annual subscriptions at a 10% commission and 70% retained_share produces $7,000 of operator revenue, not $70,000 or $10,000. Do not apply retained_share again to a figure already reported net. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis depends on control of the specified service and contractual facts; this operating model does not make every reseller arrangement an agency transaction. Reconcile the ledger presentation with the actual arrangement while preserving the scorecard's comparable retained-revenue basis. The canonical cases remain $100,000 revenue less $68,000 total modeled costs equals $32,000 owner profit; $500,000 less $275,000 equals $225,000; and $900,000 less $378,000 equals $522,000. Those are 32%, 45.0%, and 58% margins, respectively. Keep the teams at 1 FT plus 3 contractors for Conservative and Base, and 2 FT plus 4 contractors for Scaled. Neither higher billings nor more seats changes these canonical outputs.

The fourteenth trap is treating accounting profit as spendable cash while prefunding, reversals, and supplier debits move on different clocks. Customer subscription prefunding must remain traceable to its service obligations; do not use it to mask an unrelated residual shortfall. Maintain separate views of recognized retained revenue, cash receipts, customer funds supporting future delivery, reversible compensation, and remaining supplier commitments. For a clearly labeled stress case outside the canonical scorecard, a $15,000 clawback plus $20,000 of unrecovered supplier exposure reduces Base owner profit from $225,000 to $190,000 if both losses are incremental and no offsetting recovery exists. That stress case does not replace the $225,000 canonical result. Build a rolling 13-week cash forecast using actual settlement dates and contractual debit dates, not invoice issue dates. Exclude customer funds required for future supplier payments when estimating freely deployable liquidity. Trigger intervention if projected unrestricted cash cannot cover eight weeks of unavoidable operating outflows, if a supplier debit lacks assigned funding, or if a material disputed receipt is assumed collectible without supporting evidence. Freeze discretionary acquisition spend first; then curtail new commitments. Protect existing service delivery while pursuing documented recoveries, rather than financing old defects with new customer deposits.

Run a daily exception queue and a weekly contribution review that join customer, tenant, subscription, supplier order, agent registration, invoice, payment, and rebate identifiers. Pax8, Ingram, and master-agent exports can support reconciliation where available, but automation must use supported access and documented permissions. Do not give a billing script broad tenant administration rights merely because both systems mention the same customer. Restrict credentials, record changes, and alert on payout-account edits or unexplained partner reassignment. Require complete identifier coverage for new orders; investigate any orphaned supplier charge before the next payment run. Track retained contribution by customer cohort after acquisition, servicing, reversals, and collection costs. A suggested warning is a two-percentage-point decline in retained margin for two consecutive weekly closes, with immediate review for any negative-contribution cohort. Thresholds are initial operating settings, not claims about industry averages. The response sequence is containment, evidence preservation, supplier or customer correction, and controlled resumption after a clean reconciliation. Preserve original records rather than rewriting history to make dashboards agree. A small team earns its leverage by resolving exceptions early; unattended automation simply distributes the same contractual mistake across more customers.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #37, SaaS Discount Brokerage & GPO Arbitrage, ranks #04 of 37 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter organizes 12 mapped plays around renewal timing, authorized channel economics, and documented buyer demand. Start with a narrow account cohort, verify subscription commitments, and sell a bounded audit before proposing a transfer. Public signals identify questions; invoices and customer authority establish executable opportunities. A modeled 200-account cohort yields six signed mandates, with collection tracked separately. Canonical annual owner profits are $32,000 Conservative, $225,000 Base, and $522,000 Scaled. Those outcomes use retained operator revenue, never customer subscription spend. High-volume mailbox infrastructure receives an entitlement and arithmetic check rather than becoming the first-deal strategy.

sections.heading: 1. Find Renewal Pressure Before Buying Outreach Volume
paragraphs: Start with one buyer profile: organizations with 50–500 employees, a named operating or procurement owner, and a software decision expected within 120 days. Assemble 200 accounts from company websites, state business registries, public procurement calendars, SEC EDGAR filings, and referrals from bookkeepers or managed service providers. Record each source URL, observation date, business reason for contact, and confidence level in HubSpot or a controlled spreadsheet. A hiring advertisement mentioning Microsoft 365 suggests a product footprint; it does not establish seat count, renewal date, or purchasing authority. MX and SPF records can suggest messaging infrastructure, but gateways and outsourced mail services obscure the actual subscription stack. Treat DNS as a hypothesis generator, never as permission to access a tenant. Public acquisitions, office consolidations, procurement notices, and departures of procurement leaders are stronger conversation starters because they explain why ownership or demand may change. Verify the actual renewal window directly with the customer. A public bid deadline belongs to a published procurement process; it is not permission to bypass that process. Keep source collection limited to business-relevant information and avoid collecting personal identifiers that the deal does not require.

Map opportunities to the twelve plays in the matrix, then choose the smallest authorized intervention. Microsoft CSP renewal placement needs an eligible distributor relationship and customer agreement; CPOR attribution is not a universal billing-transfer mechanism. Adobe VIP Marketplace opportunities depend on the applicable reseller, anniversary, and transfer rules. Zoom and UCaaS residuals require an executed supplier or master-agent schedule through an authorized route such as Telarus or Avant. GPO rebates require genuine membership and eligible purchases, not pooled seats across unrelated tenants. Shared-savings mandates need an agreed baseline before negotiation starts. For example, a documented $120,000 renewal reduced to $96,000 produces $24,000 annual savings; a 30% contingent fee produces $7,200 operator revenue. Exclude taxes, currency changes, and scope reductions unless the mandate explicitly defines their treatment. Where supplier compensation and savings fees coexist, disclose both and document any offset. Never present illustrative channel percentages as published vendor entitlements. Obtain the current written schedule and calculate after splits, eligibility exclusions, and reversals. If an authorized route fails, retain the audit engagement or refer the implementation to a qualified partner instead of inventing a transfer pathway.

The mapped play multi_inbox_free_workspace_outbound_clusters requires a hard arithmetic and entitlement correction before use. At 300 mailboxes, 15–25 messages daily, and 22 sending days, theoretical volume is 99,000–165,000 messages monthly. Exceeding 150,000 therefore requires the upper end of that range; it says nothing about delivery or placement. At $6–$12 per seat, 300 retail seats would cost $1,800–$3,600 monthly before domains and administration. Microsoft developer subscriptions are for qualifying development activity, not an assumed subsidy for commercial prospecting. Partner benefits also require their actual permitted-use terms. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards inbound messages; it does not itself supply an outbound SMTP service. Use only expressly permitted sending accounts and relays, with accurate identity and authenticated domains. A two-to-three-domain tenant cap is an internal design choice, not proof of vendor permission. Catch-all SMTP behavior cannot verify every recipient. Remove tracking pixels, validate addresses through permitted methods, and suppress uncertain contacts. Keep standby infrastructure only for legitimate continuity, never to escape provider restrictions. The practical fallback is one branded domain, a small permission-aware account cohort, and a licensed service whose rules permit the intended outreach.

callout.title: Capture Contractual Timing, Not Merely Product Footprints
callout.body: The highest-value sourcing record combines a plausible demand signal with the contractual date that makes action possible.
items: Ask for the cancellation-notice deadline separately from the renewal date; the earlier date usually controls the usable sales window.
Maintain separate fields for CPOR attribution, reseller relationship, delegated access, and billing ownership; one does not establish the others.
Request the distributor's dated compensation schedule before quoting savings; store the eligible-charge definition alongside the percentage.
Use a customer-supplied redacted invoice for initial qualification, then request narrower contract extracts rather than an unrestricted tenant export.

sections.heading: 2. Score Executability Before Requesting a Signed Mandate
paragraphs: Use a 100-point scorecard to separate approachable accounts from executable opportunities. Allocate 20 points to renewal timing, 20 to buyer authority, 15 to baseline evidence, 20 to the authorized commercial route, 15 to retained economics, and 10 to payment exposure. Score only documented facts; an attractive logo earns nothing. Advance accounts at 75 points only when authority, entitlement, and payment requirements are independently satisfied. A prospect with a renewal in 45 days but no contract access belongs in discovery, not in the proposal forecast. Conversely, an excellent customer renewing in eight months belongs in a dated nurture queue, not a forced immediate transfer. Use task reminders at 120, 90, and 60 days before the notice deadline, adjusting for the actual supplier process. Ask five opening questions: who signs, what renews, when notice is due, what scope must remain, and who receives supplier compensation today. These questions expose incumbent relationships without accusing anyone of overcharging. Record evidence references rather than pasting full contracts into general CRM notes. Restrict document access to the owner and the specialist actually responsible for that account's authorized assessment.

Build the baseline from a dated invoice, order form, renewal quote, seat inventory, and any price-protection language. Reconcile annual commitments with monthly billing because payment frequency does not necessarily change the customer's obligation. Microsoft NCE opportunities are especially sensitive: verify the current cancellation and reduction rules for the exact subscription and transaction, then model exposure through the full enforceable term. Require prefunding or a documented payment arrangement appropriate to the exposure, with ACH or card authorization where used. Auto-debit can fail or be disputed; it is not equivalent to cash already collected. If customer credit cannot support the commitment, use an eligible direct-billing referral or an audit-only engagement. Do not fund a customer's annual obligation merely to win a thin spread. Separate list-price comparisons from actual savings: a promotional catalog discount does not prove improvement over the customer's executable renewal quote. Normalize currency, term, support, quantities, and payment dates. Retain the original baseline and a versioned adjustment log. Obtain written agreement on seat reductions, product substitutions, and implementation costs before including those items in the savings calculation.

Turn qualified demand into a narrowly scoped mandate that specifies the covered products, authorized contacts, baseline, savings percentage, measurement period, and payment trigger. A 30% fee against $24,000 verified annual savings yields $7,200, but collection timing must follow the contract rather than a sales representative's forecast. Define whether the fee becomes payable on executed renewal, realized invoice reductions, or another measurable event. Include a dispute reconciliation procedure and a deadline for delivering supporting invoices. Document channel compensation and whether it reduces the contingent charge. Obtain separate authority for distributor submissions; permission to review an invoice does not authorize a license transfer or tenant administration. Request read-only exports wherever they suffice. Never ask the buyer to email administrator credentials. An incumbent reseller objection deserves a concrete response: the audit can proceed without moving billing, and a transfer occurs only when documented economics justify disruption. When the customer refuses to share prices, offer a redacted baseline worksheet or a limited fixed-fee review instead of inventing a benchmark. Close only the service that the available evidence supports; attach later implementation work through a separately priced statement of work.

callout.title: Four Checks Before a Quote Becomes a Commitment
callout.body: A high numerical score cannot compensate for missing authority, unsupported entitlement, or unfunded obligations.
items: Verify the signer, covered customer entity, permitted data access, and separate authorization for each distributor or supplier submission.
Obtain the current CSP, VIP Marketplace, master-agent, or GPO terms supporting the precise transaction and compensation being proposed.
Reconcile the same-scope baseline, contingent fee, supplier compensation, referral split, and customer-facing disclosure in one worksheet.
Confirm available funding, enforceable collection terms, cancellation exposure, and a viable audit-only fallback before accepting annual obligations.

sections.heading: 3. Run a Bounded Multi-Channel Cadence That Earns Documents
paragraphs: Run outreach as account research followed by a specific invitation, not an inbox-count competition. The initial message should identify one observable business event, one relevant purchasing question, and one small next step. For example: 'Your procurement calendar lists a collaboration-software renewal this quarter. We compare the executable renewal quote with authorized channel options while keeping support requirements fixed. Would the owner of that renewal want a fifteen-minute scope check?' Do not claim access to private pricing or assert that DNS proves the company is overspending. Send from an identifiable business address with accurate headers, a truthful subject, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out. CAN-SPAM applies to commercial business email; follow 15 U.S.C. § 7704, including the ten-business-day opt-out deadline and applicable advertising identification. Suppress immediately operationally rather than waiting for the statutory maximum. Authenticate mail using SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, and follow the provider's acceptable-use rules. Strip tracking pixels and measure replies, meetings, and signed mandates instead of treating unreliable open rates as buyer intent. Never treat an email opt-out as an invitation to pursue the same person through another channel.

Use six touches over eighteen business days only where each channel and contact are appropriate. Begin with a researched email, follow with a manual business call, offer a useful comparison worksheet, and finish with a close-the-loop message. Stop immediately when asked, when the address is invalid, or when an applicable restriction prevents further contact. Calls and texts require separate analysis under 47 U.S.C. § 227 and 47 CFR § 64.1200; a business title does not remove protections associated with a wireless number or prohibited calling method. Do not add automated texts or prerecorded calls to this cadence without establishing the applicable permission and requirements. The FTC's Telemarketing Sales Rule contains important business-call distinctions and prohibits covered misrepresentations; avoid a blanket business-exemption assumption. Maintain channel-specific suppression and a broader do-not-contact preference when requested. Use HubSpot tasks and a shared suppression register instead of uncontrolled contractor lists. Check state calling restrictions before geographic expansion. For a small first-deal campaign, careful manual research and limited direct contact provide better learning than adding an expensive automation stack before the offer has demonstrated relevance.

Build inbound alongside outbound with a renewal-clinic page, a baseline worksheet, and one referral conversation each working day. Ask MSPs, fractional technology leaders, and bookkeeping firms for introductions to customers approaching a genuine decision, not exports of their customer databases. Publish a worked example using explicitly illustrative numbers and a defined same-scope comparison. The form should request business contact, product family, and renewal month; move contracts into a controlled upload channel after qualification. Handle objections with bounded alternatives. 'Our reseller already handles this' becomes an audit that preserves the reseller unless a better authorized outcome exists. 'We cannot change vendors' becomes a like-for-like renewal review. 'Your percentage is too high' becomes a transparent fee cap or fixed-scope diagnostic, not a hidden supplier payment. 'Send your cheapest price' becomes a request for quantities, term, support requirements, and the current executable quote. 'No time' becomes a short checklist and a scheduled date before notice expires. Record the objection category and next agreed action. A polite rejection without a future buying event belongs in closed records, not an endless automated follow-up sequence.

sections.heading: 4. Convert the First Cohort and Reconcile Every Revenue Dollar
paragraphs: Treat the initial funnel as a testable planning model rather than an industry benchmark. From 200 researched accounts, suppose 120 meet the signal definition, 60 meet timing and contact requirements, 24 produce substantive two-way conversations, 12 supply sufficient evidence and qualify, and six sign mandates. That is 60%, 50%, 40%, 50%, and 50% conversion between successive stages, or 3% from raw account to signed mandate. The 40% conversation assumption is ambitious for purely cold outreach and requires testing; warm introductions must be reported separately. Three wins from 200 accounts would be 1.5%; ten would be 5%. Define a commercial win explicitly as a signed mandate, then track accepted implementation and collected revenue as different outcomes. During weeks one and two, build evidence and obtain partner schedules. During weeks three through six, run discovery and baseline reviews. During weeks seven through twelve, close executable mandates and reconcile supplier acceptance. Some renewal calendars will exceed this window. Diagnose the stage that fails before increasing volume: poor conversations suggest relevance problems; poor document return suggests trust or effort problems; poor signatures suggest weak economics or unclear decision authority.

Keep cohort economics separate from the canonical annual scenarios. If six mandates each produce a $7,200 earned fee, the cohort yields $43,200 retained fee revenue before delivery and acquisition costs. If each customer instead produces only half the modeled savings, revenue falls to $21,600; signatures alone do not preserve the forecast. At $150 acquisition cost per signed mandate and $1,200 direct delivery cost per mandate, six completed engagements consume $8,100 and leave $35,100 before shared overhead and other costs in the full-savings illustration. These are sensitivity assumptions, not the volume scorecard. Canonical Conservative economics are $100,000 revenue less $68,000 total costs, yielding $32,000 owner profit at 32%. Base is $500,000 less $275,000, yielding $225,000 at 45.0%. Scaled is $900,000 less $378,000, yielding $522,000 at 58%. Preserve staffing of 1 FT plus 3 contractors for Conservative and Base, and 2 FT plus 4 contractors for Scaled. The stated $1,500–$9,500 monthly opex range is not a substitute for each scenario's full annual cost base. Do not backsolve it into contradictory owner-profit figures.

The scorecard revenue basis is retained operator compensation, despite its gross-revenue label; customer software billings are excluded. For an agency transaction with $100,000 underlying subscription spend and an 8% retained share, use $8,000 operator revenue, not $100,000. Apply the retained share once, not again to already-net revenue. Assess principal versus agent presentation under ASC 606 from the actual control and contractual facts; net presentation is not an elective cosmetic choice. Reconcile Pax8, Ingram, or master-agent statements against accepted customer orders, eligible charges, compensation splits, reversals, and cash receipts. Do not assume a single CPOR or VIP sync covers every distributor workflow. Use supported exports or documented interfaces and test the first transaction manually. Track rebate recognition separately from eventual payment, especially where volume brackets or customer persistence affect entitlement. Maintain a clawback register with contractual triggers and expiry dates. Expand sourcing only after one complete cycle demonstrates documented demand, authorized execution, correct fee calculation, and collection. The first ten wins should produce a reusable evidence trail and a narrower target profile, not merely a larger mailing list.

action_checklist: Build a 200-account cohort with dated public signals, a named product hypothesis, and separate fields for renewal and cancellation-notice deadlines.
Confirm current distributor, master-agent, and GPO terms; distinguish attribution, reseller status, billing control, and customer access authority.
Score each opportunity out of 100 and require documented authority, permitted execution, comparable baseline, and funded exposure before commitment.

sections.heading: 1. Turn warm renewal signals into authorized, underwritten opportunities
paragraphs: Start with an opportunity record, not a discount promise. Capture the customer entity, tenant identifier, billing owner, incumbent channel, renewal date, cancellation window, seat quantities, currency, and signed authority to inspect commercial documents. Use a customer-provided invoice and authorized administration export as primary evidence; DNS, MX, and SPF observations only suggest which questions to ask. A Microsoft mail record does not establish licensing rights or buying authority. Record the quoted SKU, commitment term, billing frequency, promotional expiry, and proposed effective date before comparing prices. Score renewal proximity at 40 points, a genuine prospect reply at 30, and observed buying authority at 30; the score prioritizes review without authorizing a purchase. Preserve an immutable source reference so repeated CRM deliveries update the work queue rather than create duplicate deals. A quote packet should identify exactly which subscriptions can move, which remain with the incumbent, and which require a new commercial agreement. If evidence conflicts, retain the existing service and ask for corrected documents. Losing a speculative spread costs less than creating overlapping annual commitments or interrupting a customer's identity, collaboration, and telephone services during an avoidable migration.

Implement high_velocity_dm_outbound_systems as a warm-trigger queue, not a mechanism for multiplying unsolicited messages. A prospect comments on a renewal checklist, reacts to an explicit offer, or initiates an inbound message; route that signal to one assigned inbox under the platform's current messaging permissions. Require the prospect's reply before sending an external booking or upload link. In Month 3, 240 eligible signals produce 120 replies, 48 discovery conversations, 24 qualified quote packets, and 20 activations after four scrubs. Those illustrative conversion rates are 50%, 40%, 50%, and 83.3% respectively, not promised platform performance. Deduplicate at the person-and-company level, honor opt-outs across inboxes, and record trigger evidence. PeerFloodError or disappearing Message Requests means stop and inspect permission and delivery conditions, not rotate identities to defeat limits. A reaction alone does not authorize every channel or message type. Telephone and text follow-up must be evaluated separately under 47 U.S.C. § 227 and 47 CFR § 64.1200. The FTC's business-to-business telemarketing treatment does not permit deceptive savings claims. Keep suppression, channel eligibility, and commercial underwriting separate so a promising renewal never overrides an outreach restriction.

Map twelve operating plays without pretending every step has a supplied registry identifier. The supplied acquisition identifier maps to warm-trigger routing; the remaining descriptive mappings are renewal-cliff scoring, authorized CSP spreads, Adobe VIP transfers, Zoom residuals, UCaaS residuals, GPO bracket rebates, shared-savings audits, license reclamation, term alignment, prefunded commitment control, and settlement recovery. Only the first identifier is asserted as registry metadata here. For each quote, calculate the retained amount after distributor charges, agent splits, and contractually required customer credits. A $12,000 customer software bill yielding a $1,200 retained spread contributes $1,200 operator revenue under the volume's net-agency basis, not $12,000. A completed savings engagement with $16,666.67 of agreed eligible savings and a 30% fee produces $5,000 after cent rounding. Define eligible savings against equivalent seats, features, support, taxes, and service periods; separate reductions caused by canceled business units. A license-reclamation recommendation can improve that baseline but earns no separate fee unless contracted. When the vendor floor removes the spread, switch to a permitted audit engagement or decline the transaction rather than pool unrelated customers' seats inside an unauthorized tenant.

sections.heading: 2. Move from signed authority to activation without inheriting unsecured commitments
paragraphs: Execute through the actual program rather than a generic partner label. Microsoft CSP resale authority, customer relationships, delegated access, subscription transfer eligibility, and CPOR associations are distinct concepts; a CPOR association is not universal permission to resell or move subscriptions. For Adobe VIP Marketplace, follow the current distributor transfer procedure and preserve the membership and order references. For Zoom or UCaaS through Telarus or Avant, verify the specific supplier agreement, commissionable products, activation event, and residual schedule. GPO work requires documented membership and the actual rebate schedule, including exclusions and customer allocations. Never assume a distributor supports an automated endpoint merely because its portal displays an operation. Use documented APIs where available and a controlled human task otherwise. Before execution, freeze the signed quote version, authorized seat counts, destination tenant, service dates, and responsible administrator. The customer retains administration rights unless separately delegated. Keep secrets out of the CRM and ledger; store credentials in a managed secret store with narrowly scoped access. If a program requires additional evidence, the opportunity waits in verification while the existing service remains intact and the quoted economics are refreshed.

Protect annual commitments before pressing the supplier order button. For an annual NCE obligation of $12,000, a customer's $1,000 monthly autodebit instruction leaves substantial exposure; it is not equivalent to prefunding the full obligation. Prefer customer-direct supplier payment where the commercial arrangement permits it, or collect cleared prefunding matched to the remaining liability. Card authorization and a newly initiated ACH debit are not cleared, irreversible funds. Document return, chargeback, and concentration exposure even after settlement. The reference workflow names its protected state funded; an escrow arrangement, when used, must be administered through an appropriately authorized provider under documented release instructions. The software state itself establishes neither custody authority nor an escrow account. Client-controlled direct payments remain evidence rather than operator cash entries; the reference client-funds postings apply only where the operator actually holds matched funds under the applicable arrangement. Maintain restricted balances separately from operating cash and never spend them on acquisition or payroll. If adequate protection is unavailable, quote an eligible monthly commitment, require a different payment structure, or decline. Do not use another customer's prepayment to bridge the shortfall.

Fulfillment ends with evidence, not an optimistic status change. Store the supplier acceptance reference, effective date, SKU quantities, customer confirmation, and first billing record. Compare the activated configuration with the frozen quote before recording an earned spread. For residuals, match each statement line to the active customer and applicable agent split. For rebates, document satisfied purchase conditions and estimate reversals only when the recognition policy supports doing so. For savings fees, the worked model assumes a distinct completed audit obligation and an enforceable fee accepted by the customer; a contingent future reduction alone is insufficient. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to each arrangement. The scorecard uses net retained operator revenue, but that convention does not determine every real contract's accounting conclusion. A reviewer should reconcile the supplier statement, customer invoice, bank receipt, and ledger event before closing a settlement period. Keep recurring relationships active across periods rather than closing them after the first commission. Correct disputed statements through documented supplier adjustments and a controlled accounting procedure; the minimal reference deliberately blocks journal edits and lacks a general credit-note subsystem. Route those exceptions outside its straight-through path until that extension is implemented and tested.

sections.heading: 3. Install the six-module ledger and serialize every consequential transition
paragraphs: Use the six reference modules below as a bounded transaction core, not an entire channel integration product. Save each artifact under its indicated filename in one directory. Initialize a fresh SQLite database with schema.sql and reconcile.sql; run python qa.py from that directory to exercise the included temporary-database checks. The reference code has not been executed here. Python 3.9 and the standard library are sufficient. Every mutation starts BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so SQLite serializes competing writers before they inspect balances or states. Unique natural identities block duplicate intake, journal source lines, workflow commands, and order creation. Integer cents eliminate binary floating-point drift, while each journal row contains one equal debit and credit. A replay returns the earlier result only when its immutable payload agrees; conflicting reuse raises an error. Keep the database on a supported local filesystem, not a shared network mount, and use SQLite's backup API for consistent snapshots. Restrict filesystem write access to the service identity because database constraints cannot replace application authorization. Rejected lock acquisition leaves no committed partial work; the caller may retry the same command identity after the contention condition clears.

Separate local atomicity from supplier-side execution. The order transition commits the workflow event, new state, and outbox row together. A worker claims that row in another serialized transaction and marks it ambiguous before touching the network. Only one worker can obtain the initial claim. Send the stable command key as the provider idempotency key where the documented API supports it. If the worker crashes before sending, or receives a timeout after sending, the item remains ambiguous and cannot be automatically claimed again. Resolve it by looking up the provider transaction or obtaining documented human confirmation. Providers without durable idempotency and lookup require this deliberately conservative halt. No local database can promise exactly-once effects across an arbitrary external service; the reference prevents duplicate local dispatch and fails closed where remote certainty is unavailable. An authenticated adapter must validate webhook signatures, supplier account scope, and source references before invoking these functions. Network calls stay outside database transactions, preventing a slow supplier from holding the writer lock. Configure alerting for pending age and ambiguous outcomes, with a named settlement owner rather than an unbounded background retry loop.

Treat the supplied core's accounting boundaries as explicit design decisions. Recognition increases receivables and retained revenue; collection increases operating cash and decreases receivables. Client funding and supplier releases affect restricted cash and client liabilities without touching revenue. Expenses reduce operating cash and owner profit. Opening owner capital is tracked separately from the operating cash-change view. The minimal engine supports a straight-through order, matched funding, positive earned fees, collections, and expenses; recurring invoice lines use distinct period-specific evidence references on an active deal. It intentionally excludes foreign exchange, tax allocation, fee reversals, partial activation, and supplier-credit accounting. Add those capabilities with explicit event types and invariant tests before routing affected production transactions through it. Store signed documents in access-controlled object storage and put stable references in the ledger; a reference string alone does not authenticate evidence. Test simultaneous duplicate delivery, changed-payload replay, insufficient funding, receipt overcollection, and interrupted provider submission. Reconcile the views to bank and supplier exports daily, then perform a restore drill against a copied backup. The included QA checks are a starting suite, not evidence that a particular deployment or adapter has passed acceptance.

PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
PRAGMA busy_timeout = 30000;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deal (
    deal_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    program TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    request_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    score INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
    exposure_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (exposure_cents >= 0),
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'intake'
        CHECK (state IN (
            'intake', 'verified', 'funded', 'authorized',
            'active', 'settled', 'rejected'
        )),
    authority_ref TEXT,
    terms_ref TEXT,
    verification_ref TEXT,
    UNIQUE (client_id, program, source_ref)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflow_event (
    command_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    deal_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES deal(deal_id),
    request_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    resulting_state TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS outbox (
    command_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES workflow_event(command_key),
    deal_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES deal(deal_id),
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
        CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'ambiguous', 'done')),
    provider_ref TEXT UNIQUE,
    UNIQUE (deal_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journal (
    event_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    deal_id TEXT REFERENCES deal(deal_id),
    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
        kind IN ('recognize', 'receipt', 'expense', 'fund', 'release', 'refund')
    ),
    amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (amount_cents > 0),
    debit_account TEXT NOT NULL,
    credit_account TEXT NOT NULL,
    evidence_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    UNIQUE (kind, evidence_ref),
    CHECK (
        (kind = 'recognize'
            AND debit_account = 'receivable'
            AND credit_account = 'revenue')
        OR (kind = 'receipt'
            AND debit_account = 'operating_cash'
            AND credit_account = 'receivable')
        OR (kind = 'expense'
            AND debit_account = 'expense'
            AND credit_account = 'operating_cash')
        OR (kind = 'fund'
            AND debit_account = 'restricted_cash'
            AND credit_account = 'client_liability')
        OR (kind IN ('release', 'refund')
            AND debit_account = 'client_liability'
            AND credit_account = 'restricted_cash')
    ),
    CHECK (kind = 'expense' OR deal_id IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON journal
BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Journal entries are immutable');
END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON journal
BEGIN
    SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Journal entries are immutable');
END;
Unique source references and balanced two-account entries prevent duplicate local records
Execute against a fresh local database before accepting any production commands
Module 2 — intake.py scores opportunities and provides serialized transaction boundaries

import json
import sqlite3
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager


@contextmanager
def transaction(path):
    con = sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    con.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    con.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 30000")
    try:
        con.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        yield con
        con.commit()
    except BaseException:
        if con.in_transaction:
            con.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        con.close()


def intake(path, client_id, program, source_ref, days_to_renewal,
           replied, authority_seen, exposure_cents):
    if not all(isinstance(x, str) and x.strip()
               for x in (client_id, program, source_ref)):
        raise ValueError("Client, program, and source references are required")
    if type(exposure_cents) is not int or exposure_cents < 0:
        raise ValueError("Exposure must be nonnegative integer cents")
    if type(days_to_renewal) is not int:
        raise ValueError("Renewal distance must be an integer")
    if type(replied) is not bool or type(authority_seen) is not bool:
        raise ValueError("Signal inputs must be boolean values")
    request = json.dumps(
        [client_id, program, source_ref, days_to_renewal,
         replied, authority_seen, exposure_cents],
        separators=(",", ":"),
    )
    identity = json.dumps(
        [client_id, program, source_ref], separators=(",", ":")
    )
    deal_id = str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_URL, identity))
    score = (
        40 * (0 <= days_to_renewal <= 90)
        + 30 * replied
        + 30 * authority_seen
    )
    with transaction(path) as con:
        prior = con.execute(
            "SELECT request_json FROM deal WHERE deal_id = ?", (deal_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if prior:
            if prior[0] != request:
                raise ValueError("Intake identity reused with different inputs")
            return deal_id
        con.execute(
            """INSERT INTO deal
               (deal_id, client_id, program, source_ref, request_json,
                score, exposure_cents)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (deal_id, client_id, program, source_ref,
             request, score, exposure_cents),
        )
    return deal_id
Deterministic deal identity and locked comparisons reject changed-payload intake replays
Invoke only behind authenticated intake handling with validated customer evidence

One claimed outbox item prevents competing workers from submitting the initial order
Connect an authorized supplier adapter and investigate ambiguous outcomes before continuing
Module 4 — settlement.py posts retained revenue and segregated client funding
Locked balance checks prevent overcollection and disbursement beyond recorded client funds
Validate bank and supplier evidence before calling the journal posting function
Module 5 — reconcile.sql exposes deal balances and owner cash conversion

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS deal_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    d.deal_id,
    d.client_id,
    d.program,
    d.state,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN j.kind = 'recognize'
        THEN j.amount_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS revenue_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN j.kind = 'receipt'
        THEN j.amount_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS collected_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE
        WHEN j.kind = 'recognize' THEN j.amount_cents
        WHEN j.kind = 'receipt' THEN -j.amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END), 0) AS receivable_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE
        WHEN j.kind = 'fund' THEN j.amount_cents
        WHEN j.kind IN ('release', 'refund') THEN -j.amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END), 0) AS client_funds_cents
FROM deal d
LEFT JOIN journal j ON j.deal_id = d.deal_id
GROUP BY d.deal_id, d.client_id, d.program, d.state;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS operator_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'recognize'
        THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS revenue_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'expense'
        THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END), 0) AS expense_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE
        WHEN kind = 'recognize' THEN amount_cents
        WHEN kind = 'expense' THEN -amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END), 0) AS owner_profit_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE
        WHEN kind = 'receipt' THEN amount_cents
        WHEN kind = 'expense' THEN -amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END), 0) AS operating_cash_change_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(CASE
        WHEN kind = 'recognize' THEN amount_cents
        WHEN kind = 'receipt' THEN -amount_cents
        ELSE 0 END), 0) AS receivable_cents
FROM journal;
Client subscription funding never enters recognized revenue or operating cash change
Compare daily exports against source statements and investigate every unmatched difference
Module 6 — qa.py exercises concurrent replay and straight-through settlement

import sqlite3
import tempfile
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from intake import intake, transaction
from workflow import apply, claim_order, finish_order
from settlement import post


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)


def audit(path):
    with transaction(path) as con:
        require(
            con.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] == "ok",
            "SQLite integrity check failed",
        )
        require(
            not con.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall(),
            "Foreign key check failed",
        )
        require(
            not con.execute(
                """SELECT deal_id FROM deal_reconciliation
                   WHERE receivable_cents < 0 OR client_funds_cents < 0"""
            ).fetchall(),
            "Client balance invariant failed",
        )
        require(
            not con.execute(
                """SELECT d.deal_id FROM deal d
                   JOIN deal_reconciliation r USING (deal_id)
                   WHERE d.state IN ('funded', 'authorized')
                     AND r.client_funds_cents < d.exposure_cents"""
            ).fetchall(),
            "Reserved exposure lacks client funding",
        )
        require(
            not con.execute(
                "SELECT command_key FROM outbox WHERE status = 'ambiguous'"
            ).fetchall(),
            "Provider submission requires receipt investigation",
        )
        revenue, expense, profit, cash, receivable = con.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM operator_reconciliation"
        ).fetchone()
        require(revenue - expense == profit, "Profit equation failed")
        require(profit - cash == receivable, "Cash bridge failed")


def self_test():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        path = str(Path(directory) / "ledger.sqlite3")
        con = sqlite3.connect(path)
        try:
            con.executescript(Path("schema.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            con.executescript(Path("reconcile.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        finally:
            con.close()

        def same_intake(_):
            return intake(
                path, "client-001", "authorized-csp", "renewal-001",
                45, True, True, 100000,
            )

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
            identities = list(pool.map(same_intake, range(32)))
        require(len(set(identities)) == 1, "Concurrent intake duplicated a deal")
        deal_id = identities[0]
        apply(path, "verify-001", deal_id, "verify",
              "review-001", "authority-001", "terms-001")
        post(path, "fund-001", deal_id, "fund", 100000, "bank-credit-001")
        apply(path, "reserve-001", deal_id, "reserve", "exposure-check-001")
        apply(path, "order-001", deal_id, "order", "signed-quote-001")
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
            claims = list(pool.map(
                lambda _: claim_order(path, "order-001"), range(32)
            ))
        require(
            sum(claim is not None for claim in claims) == 1,
            "More than one worker claimed the same order",
        )
        finish_order(path, "order-001", "provider-activation-001")
        apply(path, "confirm-001", deal_id, "confirm",
              "provider-activation-001")
        post(path, "release-001", deal_id, "release",
             100000, "supplier-settlement-001")
        post(path, "fee-001", deal_id, "recognize", 10000, "invoice-line-001")

        def same_receipt(_):
            post(path, "receipt-001", deal_id, "receipt",
                 10000, "bank-receipt-001")

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
            list(pool.map(same_receipt, range(32)))
        try:
            post(path, "receipt-001", deal_id, "receipt",
                 9999, "bank-receipt-001")
        except ValueError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Conflicting replay was accepted")
        apply(path, "close-001", deal_id, "close", "close-package-001")
        audit(path)
        with transaction(path) as con:
            require(
                con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deal").fetchone()[0] == 1,
                "Intake uniqueness failed",
            )
            require(
                con.execute(
                    "SELECT revenue_cents FROM operator_reconciliation"
                ).fetchone()[0] == 10000,
                "Revenue was duplicated",
            )
    print("Reference concurrency, replay, and reconciliation checks passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    self_test()
Concurrent duplicate commands yield one deal, one initial order claim, and one receipt
Run locally, add failure-injection tests, and record actual deployment acceptance results

sections.heading: 4. Walk the first ninety days from qualified signals to reconciled cash
paragraphs: The cohort below starts with $20,000 owner capital, no opening receivables, and no preexisting recurring book. All operating expenses are paid in the month incurred; client subscription cash is excluded. Month 1 converts 120 warm signals into 60 replies, 24 discoveries, 12 qualified opportunities, and ten activations after two scrubs. Six reseller accounts contribute $500 each, two residual accounts contribute $500 each, one rebate contributes $1,000, and one completed savings audit contributes $5,000: total recognized revenue is $10,000. Month 2 adds fifteen activations from eighteen qualified opportunities. Eight reseller accounts at $750, three residual accounts at $500, two rebates at $1,750, and two audits at $5,000 generate $21,000 new revenue. Add the first month's $4,000 recurring spread-and-residual book to reach $25,000. Rebate and audit amounts do not automatically recur. Scrubs happen before ordering and recognition, so the model does not bury their lost forecast value inside realized revenue. Acquisition and contractor expenses still absorb the work spent on those rejected opportunities. The example assumes no defaults or post-activation clawbacks; replacing that assumption requires an explicit loss expense and revised cash bridge.

Month 3 adds twenty activations: ten reseller accounts at $800, four residual accounts at $750, three earned rebates at $1,388.89, and three completed audits at $5,000. New revenue equals $30,166.67. The retained recurring book contributes another $11,500 from Months 1 and 2, producing $41,666.67 recognized revenue. All six audits across the quarter use a 30% fee on $16,666.67 accepted eligible savings, rounded to $5,000 apiece. The model assumes the contracted audit obligation is completed and collectible in its stated month. Fixed monthly overhead is $6,500, within the volume's $1,500–$9,500 monthly overhead range. Delivery labor, commissions, payment costs, and other variable operating costs equal 39.4% of recognized revenue in this illustration. Therefore Month 3 variable costs are $16,416.67 and total costs are $22,916.67, leaving $18,750 owner profit. The Base team remains one full-time owner plus three contractors; contractor costs are included rather than hidden outside the margin. The $500,000 annual revenue and $275,000 annual cost targets imply $225,000 profit at 45.0%. Month 3 is a replenished operating pace, not contracted recurring revenue or a claim that the ramp quarter already earned one quarter of the annual target.

Cash conversion determines the safe distribution, not the revenue dashboard. Month 1 collects $6,000 and carries $4,000 receivables. Month 2 collects that $4,000 plus $18,000 of current fees, ending with $7,000 receivables. Month 3 collects the $7,000 opening balance plus $31,666.67 current fees, leaving $10,000 receivables. Quarter collections total $66,666.67 against $49,706.67 paid operating costs, so cumulative operating cash generation is $16,960. Quarter recognized revenue of $76,666.67 less those costs produces $26,960 owner profit; the $10,000 difference is closing receivables. Add the initial $20,000 capital to obtain $36,960 closing unrestricted cash before owner distributions. Restricted customer funds, if any, sit outside that number. For annual reconciliation, use exact annual targets rather than multiplying rounded monthly displays: eight revenue months at $41,666.67 and four at $41,666.66 total $500,000. Apply the corresponding cent allocation to annual costs to preserve $225,000 profit. Conservative remains $100,000 revenue, $68,000 costs, and $32,000 profit; Scaled remains $900,000 revenue, $378,000 costs, and $522,000 profit. None of these scenarios counts customer software spend as operator revenue or reuses the same rebate twice.

This chapter maps 12 operator plays across public-record qualification, authorized tenant diagnostics, partner settlement, GPO rebates, shared-savings audits, and startup-credit eligibility. An eighteen-entry resource directory separates observable facts from sales hypotheses and specifies access, spending controls, refresh targets, and fallback evidence. sections.heading: 1. Establish the legal buyer and evidence hierarchy before purchasing enrichment
paragraphs: The first three mapped plays are Legal-Entity Qualification, Public-Procurement Triggering, and Renewal-Evidence Acquisition. Start with the contracting entity, not an attractive domain. Delaware and Wyoming registries establish filed names and status; neither proves beneficial ownership, operational substance, or eligibility for a vendor incentive. SEC EDGAR adds dated acquisition disclosures, subsidiary exhibits, and material agreements for reporting companies. SAM.gov and USAspending.gov expose registration and award context, but an award amount is neither software budget nor available brokerage revenue. Store each observation with source URL, retrieval timestamp, effective date, entity identifier, and permitted use. A domain-to-company match becomes usable only after a second independent identifier agrees, such as a customer-provided registration number or a signed order naming the same entity. For a batch of 200 businesses, suppose 120 identity matches survive review and 30 supply actual subscription documents. The yield is 15% document-qualified accounts, not 200 opportunities. If public records conflict with an invoice, suspend the proposed transfer and request the current contracting-party document. This prevents commissions being attributed to a similarly named affiliate and stops unsupported assumptions about group purchasing eligibility from entering the proposal.

Use public purchasing evidence to select questions, not manufacture precision. A GSA eLibrary contractor listing can identify an authorized schedule holder and relevant contract categories; its existence does not establish that a private buyer receives federal pricing. A USAspending award modification may suggest implementation activity, while the actual order, scope, and option period determine timing. Attach an evidence grade to each renewal field: executed contract, authenticated billing export, buyer confirmation, or inferred signal. Only the first two should drive an irreversible purchase commitment. Consider 40 leads researched at six minutes each: four hours at a loaded $40 hourly cost equals $160 before enrichment charges. If eight buyers provide contracts, research costs $20 per document-qualified account. Compare that figure with expected retained contribution, not the customer's annual software spend. A $24,000 subscription yielding an illustrative 8% retained spread produces $1,920 before servicing costs and reversals. Losing the customer after three paid months reduces that simple annualized expectation to $480. Maintain the original document beside every extracted renewal date so a reviewer can distinguish an anniversary, cancellation deadline, billing date, and price-protection expiry without reconstructing the research trail.

Build the first six directory entries into a narrow acquisition pipeline. Use PostgreSQL for durable records, object storage for permissioned source documents, and a scheduled worker for refreshes; SQLite is sufficient for an initial single-operator desk. Separate source_changed_at from retrieved_at because a freshly downloaded record may still describe an old event. Hash document bytes, retain extraction version numbers, and preserve corrected values as new observations rather than silently overwriting history. Source costs and limits below are procurement categories and operator refresh targets, not live vendor quotations or promises of publication speed. Registry interfaces change, and some states charge separately for certificates or detailed reports. Before enabling a connector, capture its current terms, authentication method, documented limits, and assigned internal owner. Under 18 U.S.C. 1030, do not treat a visible login screen or guessed endpoint as permission to retrieve protected records. When automation is unavailable, use a permitted manual lookup or obtain the document directly from the buyer. Weekly refreshes usually suffice for entity status; contract deadlines require explicit calendar monitoring. Delete unnecessary personal information rather than turning a lean brokerage ledger into an indiscriminate contact archive.

sections.heading: 2. Turn technographic hints into authorized, measurable renewal evidence
paragraphs: The next three mapped plays are DNS/MX/SPF Technographic Qualification, Licensed Enrichment Waterfalls, and Authorized Tenant Seat Diagnostics. Query public DNS with dig or a documented DNS-over-HTTPS service to identify mail-routing and sender-policy clues. Microsoft-oriented MX records suggest a mail environment, not the customer's license edition, seat count, reseller, or renewal date. SPF includes may represent dormant tooling or a third-party sender rather than an active paid subscription. RDAP supplies domain registration context, with substantial redaction and no reliable purchasing authority. BuiltWith can add website technology observations; Hunter can help locate business contact information under its permitted-use terms. Run the waterfall in that order only when each additional field improves a defined decision. If 500 domains receive free DNS checks, 150 need a hypothetical $0.10 technology lookup, and 50 need a hypothetical $0.20 contact lookup, variable data cost is $25. Those prices are planning assumptions, not vendor quotes. Stop enrichment when the buyer is already reachable. A missing field should route to direct buyer confirmation, not another opaque data broker. Preserve observation age so abandoned technologies do not masquerade as current negotiation leverage during renewal outreach.

Tenant diagnostics begin only after the customer authorizes the required access. Microsoft Graph GET /v1.0/subscribedSkus can expose subscribed products and capacity under documented permissions; it does not by itself establish cancellation rights or commercial renewal terms. Obtain the least privileged current permission that supports the endpoint, and keep each customer's tokens and exports isolated. Google Admin SDK Directory API users.list can support account inventory with administrator authorization; user existence is not proof of a paid Workspace license or recent usage. Combine authorized inventory, appropriate usage reports, and billing exports instead of equating inactive identities with removable seats. Suppose a customer has 80 seats at an illustrative $30 monthly unit price, with 12 candidates for removal. The ceiling on annual list-price reduction is 12 × $30 × 12 = $4,320, but an annual commitment may defer every dollar until renewal. At a contracted 30% shared-savings fee, fully realized eligible savings would generate $1,296. If the customer must retain four seats, the comparable ceiling falls to $2,880 and the fee to $864. Obtain service-owner confirmation before recommending deletion, reassignment, or a lower product tier.

Represent enrichment as evidence events rather than one mutable company profile. Each event should contain tenant scope, source system, observed value, observation time, confidence basis, retention deadline, and extraction version. For network diagnostics, constrain activity to ordinary public queries; do not enumerate protected tenant resources, test passwords, or probe customer applications without separate authorization. Build retries around documented response codes, exponential backoff, jitter, and a per-provider concurrency ceiling. Honor Retry-After when supplied, and never rotate accounts to defeat quotas. Cache DNS responses within their TTL, deduplicate enrichment purchases, and attach a budget ceiling to each research batch. Test connectors using synthetic customer identifiers and redacted fixtures; retain enough provenance to explain why a particular contact was approached. Outreach requires its own controls: 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200 govern covered calling and texting activity, while 16 CFR Part 310 includes relevant restrictions on deceptive B2B telemarketing. Do not assume a business label removes every restriction. For commercial email, implement accurate sender information and working opt-out processing under 15 U.S.C. 7704. Suppress opted-out contacts across every enrichment provider before the next campaign export.
